name: Huey P. Newton
role: Co-founder and Minister of Defense of the Black Panther Party (1966-1989)
summary: Co-founded the Black Panther Party for Self-Defense and developed its ideology from Black nationalism through revolutionary nationalism to revolutionary intercommunalism, a Marxist-influenced view of a world-wide struggle against a US-led empire. He favored community control of the means of production, a guaranteed livelihood, armed self-defense against police, a disciplined vanguard party and survival programs, and by 1970 urged alliance with the women's and gay liberation movements.

public-ownership.rationale: Ten-Point Program: if businessmen will not give full employment, the means of production should be taken from them and placed in the community or the people's hands.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rejected capitalism as the cause of oppression and wanted the means of production taken from private owners; said only a planned economy could handle the chaos of ending war production.

property-fundamental.rationale: Called for seizing the means of production and turning landlords' housing into cooperatives; wanted administrators serving the people, not private property.

cut-welfare.rationale: Held that the federal government must provide every person employment or a guaranteed income, and that those who cannot work deserve a high standard of living.

worker-ownership.rationale: Wanted the community to take over the means of production and choose managers; the ownership is community-wide rather than strictly by each firm's workers.

state-harmful.rationale: Argued that the state will not disappear until imperialism is destroyed, and criticized anarchists for wanting to go straight from state to no state.

limit-guns.rationale: Led the Party's armed patrols, said all Black people should arm themselves under the Second Amendment, and opposed the 1967 Mulford gun bill.

empower-police-military.rationale: Called the police an occupying army in Black communities and demanded they withdraw; opposed military power used abroad.

decide-locally.rationale: Demanded power for Black communities to determine their own destiny and a police force made up of community members; also called for worldwide unity of communities.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Demanded forty acres and two mules as overdue restitution for slavery and later urged keeping race-conscious affirmative action.

gradual-change.rationale: Held revolution is a justified process of qualitative leaps, and criticized the Black bourgeois politics of working within existing institutions.

nation-first.rationale: Called for a united worldwide struggle of the oppressed and redistribution of the world's wealth, with the US ruling circle as the enemy of all peoples.

open-borders.rationale: Said the hope for freedom lay in a future with the elimination of national boundaries and ties, a world without boundary lines.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Said technology can solve most of the material contradictions people face, provided the people control it rather than the ruling circle.

revolution-justified.rationale: Wrote that the people may and should overthrow oppressive government and made revolution the Party's stated aim.

central-planning.rationale: Said a planned economy was needed to manage the transition when war production ends and called for the people's control of the means of production.

basic-income.rationale: Said the government is obliged to provide employment or a guaranteed income, and a high standard of living for those who cannot work; this is not an unconditional payment to all adults.

one-party-rule.rationale: Led a vanguard party and recognized the single-party governments of China, North Korea and North Vietnam as the people's governments, but also argued for community participation.

democracy-best.rationale: Called American bourgeois democracy domination of the majority over the minority and said democracy means fair shares and control over administrators, not just ballots.

political-violence-never.rationale: Argued that when peaceful politics fails it continues as war and that armed self-defense and guerrilla action are justified.

military-superiority.rationale: Condemned the US military-industrial empire and its Pentagon contracts and backed the peace movement.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Said the Party gave up separatist nationalism in favor of internationalism and intercommunalism, since nation-states were no longer a viable solution.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Described class conflict between owners and workers as developing by the same dialectical principles as all change, alongside racial caste oppression.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Said every person has a right to share in the wealth, and a high standard of living regardless of education or skill.

restore-past-order.rationale: Aimed at a revolutionary transformation toward communism and rejected static reliance on the past.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Insisted on concrete analysis of concrete conditions and merging theory with practice, but also called ideology the most important part of the Party's thinking.

direct-action.rationale: Said that participating in the American democratic process does not serve the Black community and built the Party around self-defense power and survival programs.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Looked to a world where people share all the wealth they produce and each person is guaranteed a livelihood whatever his skill.

production-for-use.rationale: Wanted the economy run for the people's livelihood and not the interest of private property, and condemned war production for profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Wrote that the prison and capitalist system rests on exploiters who profit from the poverty of those at the bottom.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Argued that capitalism, when it cannot expand, invests in the Pentagon and foreign wars such as Vietnam, leading to a warfare state.

conscription.rationale: Ten-Point Program demanded exemption of Black men from military service and refused to fight other people of color for a racist government.

positive-liberty.rationale: Argued that political rights meant little without land, economic power and the means to act, citing forty acres and two mules.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Wrote that Black disadvantage came from a hostile social system and lack of opportunity and early advantages, not from lack of innate ability.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Condemned US expansion and intervention abroad as imperialist counterrevolution.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Called for the people to choose managers who control the means of production in the people's interest.

national-self-determination.rationale: Wrote in 1974 that the right of nations to self-determination is recognized in the Declaration of Independence and that US policy violated it.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Grounded Party ideology in materialism and the scientific method, though he said the materialist premise was an arbitrary choice and valued subjective commitment.

class-collaboration.rationale: Treated the owner and worker classes as opposed and capitalist exploitation as the cause of oppression, while seeing small Black capitalists as partly redeemable.

dominated-front.rationale: Called for a united, worldwide thrust of the oppressed against the US ruling circle and the unity of all oppressed people.

workers-nation.rationale: Called the Party internationalist and said Black Americans are the first real internationalists; envisioned world revolution and one world community.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Led a Party organized against racist law and police and demanded equal justice and juries of peers, and rejected separation as a solution.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Described the state as a hierarchy that limits individuals in a class society and said all state administrations oppress someone.

national-mission.rationale: Wrote that the US had consistently crushed other peoples' revolutions in violation of their self-determination.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Called women an oppressed group, said they are probably oppressed, and urged revolutionaries to support women's liberation.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Said slick politicians and exploitative educators mislead the people and that a small ruling circle rules the US in its own interest.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Demanded that government guarantee employment, housing and other services and take over production if businesses fail.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wrote that exploited and exploiters have no sacredness over each other, and that all people are as worthy and dignified, adding respect for all oppressed people.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Said even liberated territories cannot be sovereign while the US holds war technology, and criticized the Soviet Union's peaceful coexistence.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Said the state will not disappear until imperialism is wiped out, citing Cuba's disciplined vanguard.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Ten-Point Program he co-wrote closes by quoting that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Defended armed self-defense and revolution against an oppressor, rather than treating all initiated force as wrong; said only a humane revolution is worth fighting.

vanguard-party.rationale: Wrote that a vanguard party must lead and teach the masses correct strategy, and that revolution requires a dedicated cadre and structure.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Built the Party's program and survival programs around the needs of poor Black people and demanded guaranteed livelihood.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Said capitalist exploitation is one of the basic causes of the community's problems.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Described deferring to Central Committee votes: after the vote he supported the Party position until the next meeting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Called for Black people to arm themselves house to house and community to community and warned police to face the wrath of the armed people.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Said revolutionary nationalists seek revolutionary change including the economic system and that Reconstruction failed without land and economic power.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Called a People's Revolutionary Constitutional Convention in 1970 to write a new constitution; the call is not specific about election of delegates.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Called for redistributing the world's wealth, while warning that US foreign aid was used to discredit socialism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said the economy's controllers must be judged by furnishing a livelihood and lose control otherwise, with people-chosen administrators serving the people not private property.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Called the Soviet Union the First Workers State while criticizing its peaceful coexistence line as a mistake or betrayal.

character-from-environment.rationale: Wrote that most human behavior is learned and that early home and school conditions shape a person's self-image, not instinct.

land-redistribution.rationale: Demanded forty acres and two mules and said that without land Black people have no power; wanted the land placed in people's hands.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Said nationhood by separation was unattainable and the struggle had to be within the US, rejecting separate communities as a solution.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Chose dialectical materialism as the Party's method and tied political change to economic and technological development.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: In 1967 advocated vanguard guerrilla example, but later called heroes isolated from the people and said revolution is a process led through community programs.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Condemned colonialism and the extraction of labor and resources by settlers and administrators.

patriotic-education.rationale: Demanded education that exposes the true nature of a decadent American society and refused to defend a racist government.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Wrote to the NAACP and University of California to defend the special admissions program in the Bakke case.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Said all Americans are exploited by a few giant firms, but also that fully employed workers are bought off with the highest wages in the world.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The Ten-Point Program quotes the Declaration: when a government is destructive it is the people's right and duty to throw it off.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Argued that politics is war without bloodshed and built the Party to take political action.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Said the people's opinions are molded against their own interests by politicians and educators, in addition to force.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Wrote that US capitalists built technology through expropriation of the world and dominate it by robbing the world's goods.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Told Buckley that Westerners define democracy by the ballot and that other cultures define it differently, saying Chinese talks had shown how Western-brainwashed he had been.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Criticized military coups and army regimes serving the Pentagon in developing countries.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Wrote that after prison he was no longer dependent on the things of the world, and that prisoners chasing money, power and conspicuous consumption are illegitimate capitalists.

corporate-influence.rationale: Said super-capitalists marry industry to the Pentagon and that seventy-six firms control the economy.

job-guarantee.rationale: Ten-Point Program says the federal government is obligated to give every man employment or a guaranteed income.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Wrote that people should not respect rules that do not serve them and that the poor have the duty to write their own rules.

informal-organisation.rationale: Argued that anarchists without disciplined organization cannot defeat the organized state and that a disciplined vanguard is needed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Denounced US domination as an empire that every people must resist.

defeat-communism.rationale: Praised China, North Korea and the liberated zones of Vietnam and called for the people's seizure of the means of production toward communism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Said people create God in their own image, but also sought partnership with the Black church.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Said imperialism laid the foundation for world communism and that technology gives socialism its base.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Described the world as dispersed communities with comprehensive institutions and wanted housing cooperatives, though his end goal was one world community.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Called capitalism no solution and aimed for communism, rejecting a third course.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The Ten-Point Program states that the Germans murdered six million Jews.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Wrote that homosexuals are not enemies of the people, may be revolutionaries, and should have freedom to use their bodies as they choose.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Condemned colonial extraction in the world analysis of empire and demanded liberation for colonized peoples.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Insisted people define and control phenomena in their own communities and choose their administrators and managers.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Said racism, women's oppression and chauvinism must be resolved together and that isolating women and gay people weakens revolutionary groups.

alienated-labor.rationale: Described slavery followed by wage slavery as the base of expropriation of the worker's product.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rejected capitalism as exploitation and wanted production taken into the people's hands.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Said a handful of super-capitalists who control the economy rule the country.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Wanted the police to be the people of the community in uniform, rather than abolishing police.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Held that government must provide a livelihood and described Party survival programs as stopgaps rather than answers.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Condemned private ownership profit as exploitation and tied the right to share in wealth to being a person.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Argued the right to armed self-defense against police violence and said each person has an obligation to preserve himself.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Chose materialist premises as the Party's ideology: the world began as matter and motion, not spirit.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Said the people must seize the means of production and all social institutions to establish communism.

municipal-property.rationale: Ten-Point Program proposed putting the means of production and housing in community ownership as cooperatives.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Held materialist premises but wrote that in prison he found a higher freedom and that submission would have killed his spirit.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Built a Black-led party to serve the interests of the Black community, while later urging coalitions.

racial-pride.rationale: Ten-Point Program demanded education giving Black people self-knowledge and said Black people had been taught to feel inferior.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Demanded that Black people arm themselves for self-defense against police and army.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Ten-Point Program says Black men will not fight and kill other people of color for a racist government.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Called for redistributing the world's wealth and criticized trade and aid as tools of US domination.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Called for seizing the machinery of power from the ruling circle and replacing it with the people's provisional governments.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Described Black communities as a dispersed colony in 1971 but said in 1972 that Black Americans are not colonial subjects strictly speaking.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Recognized the liberated governments of China, North Korea and North Vietnam and said the world must follow them.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Demanded an end to police murder of Black people and condemned police killings.

self-ownership.rationale: Wrote that a person should be free to use his body however he wishes, in the context of gay liberation.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Said a political vehicle must stand between the people and their oppressors and articulate their interests.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Said that democracy should be judged by fair share and control over administrators, not the ballot box.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Wrote that Black oppression is economic with racism at its base and that racist institutions persist.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Wrote that rules which do not serve the people deserve no respect.

material-over-identity.rationale: Pushed for coalitions with women's and gay liberation movements as revolutionary allies.

notes: Positions changed from separatist Black nationalism (1966) to internationalism and intercommunalism (1970-71). The 1971 Cleaver split led him to criticize revolutionary cultism and military adventurism. Statements on topics he never addressed (healthcare, abortion, drugs policy, death penalty, religion in public life) stay null.
